excerpts.text: Learning objectives: describe the median, explain simple linear regression, and describe bootstrap resampling.
Order the observations. For an odd number of observations, the median is the middle observation. For an even number, it is the average of the two central observations.
Simple linear regression uses a straight-line model to describe a response variable in terms of one explanatory variable.
A bootstrap resample draws observations with replacement from the observed sample, retaining its size. Recompute a statistic on each of many such resamples to investigate its sampling variability.

full_reviewed_notes.e2: The median is a middle value of an ordered data set. With an odd number of observations use the middle observation; with an even number use the average of the two central observations. This is a definition, not a worked calculation.
full_reviewed_notes.e3: Simple linear regression describes a response using one explanatory variable and a straight-line model. The passage is conceptual and specifies no software. It does not discuss multiple-predictor models.
full_reviewed_notes.e4: A bootstrap resample draws observations with replacement from the observed sample, normally retaining its size. Repeating this produces a collection of recomputed statistics used to investigate sampling variability. The passage explains resampling rather than defining an average.
